Extraction of genomic DNA: extract genomic DNA from the samples using standard methods. Note: The purity of the obtained DNA sample is critical for the next quantification step. It is recommended to use commercial kits that yield PCR-compatible DNA. We usually use the FavorPrep Blood Genomic DNA Extraction kit for culture cells and the FavorPrep Tissue Genomic DNA Extraction kit for tumor tissue masses. However, kits from other manufacturers (e.g., QIAamp DNA kit from Qiagen) also work well. For culture cells, purification using SPRI beads can also be performed [14].
Relative knock-in efficiency = 2^(-ΔΔCt) C

steps.title: Prepare PEI Max transfection solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 100 mg PEI MAX (5 mg/mL stock) in 1 N NaOH, adjust pH to 7.6, then bring the volume to 20 mL with distilled water.

steps.title: Prepare qPCR reaction mix
steps.instruction: For each 20 µL reaction combine 10 µL 1× GoTaq qPCR master mix, 0.4 µL forward primer (10 µM, final 200 nM), 0.4 µL reverse primer (10 µM, final 200 nM), 1–5 µL template DNA (10–50 ng), and add water to 20 µL.

steps.title: Seed adherent cells
steps.instruction: Plate cells in 3.5 cm dishes; use ~1 × 10⁴ cells/dish for HeLa or 5–10 × 10⁴ cells/dish for slower lines so they reach 80–90 % confluency at harvest.

steps.title: Incubate cells 24 h
steps.instruction: Place dishes in a 5 % CO₂ incubator at 37 °C for 24 hours.

steps.title: Optional siRNA / plasmid transfection
steps.instruction: For each dish add 200 µL Opti‑MEM, 10 pmol siRNA, 0.5 µg expression plasmid, and 2–4 µL TransIT‑X2; mix, incubate 37 °C 30 min, then add to cells.

substeps.instruction: If evaluating GOI knock‑down, perform siRNA transfection one day before ASHRA plasmids.
Titrate siRNA and reagent amounts for each experiment.

steps.title: Post‑siRNA incubation and medium change
steps.instruction: Incubate transfected cells for another 24 h, then replace with fresh growth medium before ASHRA plasmid transfection.

steps.title: Transfect ASHRA plasmids into adherent cells
steps.instruction: For each dish add 200 µL Opti‑MEM, 0.5 µg LentiCRISPRv2‑ACTB‑C1 (or scr) plasmid, 0.5 µg pBS‑ACTB‑C200‑GFPfr1 donor plasmid, then add 1 µL PEI Max solution; mix, incubate 37 °C 30 min, and add to cells.

substeps.instruction: Alternative transfection reagents (e.g., other PEI formulations) may be used.
Alternative plasmid versions (e.g., LentiCRISPRv2‑ACTB‑C4) are acceptable.

steps.title: Incubate transfected adherent cells
steps.instruction: Return dishes to the 5 % CO₂ incubator at 37 °C for 48–72 h (48 h for fast‑growing lines like HeLa, up to 72 h for slower lines).

steps.title: Prepare suspension cells for electroporation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge cells at 500 × g, 5 min, RT; discard supernatant; rinse with 5 mL Opti‑MEM and repeat centrifugation; resuspend in 1–2 mL Opti‑MEM, count, then aliquot 1 × 10⁴ cells into a tube, centrifuge 500 × g 5 min, discard supernatant, and resuspend in 100 µL Opti‑MEM.

steps.title: Electroporate suspension cells
steps.instruction: Add 10 µg total ASHRA plasmids (Cas9/gRNA + donor; optional siRNA/plasmid) to the 100 µL cell suspension, apply NEPA21 pulse (125 V, 2 ms, 6 repeats, polarity –), immediately cool on ice 1 min, then transfer cells to pre‑warmed growth medium in a 3.5 cm dish.

substeps.instruction: Electroporation conditions may need titration for each cell line.

steps.title: Incubate electroporated suspension cells
steps.instruction: Culture the cells in a 5 % CO₂ incubator at 37 °C for 48–72 h.

steps.title: Prepare tumor tissue specimens
steps.instruction: Grow tumors (≈1 cm diameter) in immunocompromised mice, optionally treat with drug (e.g., doxycycline), surgically excise, and trim to ~150 mm³ (≈5 mm cube).

steps.title: Inject plasmid solution and electroporate tumor tissue
steps.instruction: Inject 0.1–0.2 mL of 100 µg/mL ASHRA plasmid solution (add indigo carmine ≤1 mg/mL if desired) into the tissue with a 1 mL syringe, 29 G needle; rinse with 5 % glucose solution; apply NEPA21 forceps‑type pulse (125 V, 5 ms, 2 repeats, polarity +).

substeps.instruction: Multiple injections may be needed for even distribution.

steps.title: Incubate electroporated tumor tissue
steps.instruction: Place specimens in DMEM containing 8 % FBS (or appropriate medium) and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 72 h, ensuring they are fully immersed in medium immediately after electroporation.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Use FavorPrep Blood Genomic DNA Extraction Mini kit for cultured cells or FavorPrep Tissue Genomic DNA Extraction Mini kit for tumor samples (alternatives such as QIAamp DNA kit are acceptable); follow the manufacturer’s protocol to obtain PCR‑compatible DNA.

steps.title: Measure and normalize DNA concentration
steps.instruction: Determine DNA concentration by UV absorbance or fluorescent dye assay; if concentrations differ markedly, dilute or concentrate samples so that all reactions contain comparable DNA amounts.

steps.title: Set up and run quantitative PCR
steps.instruction: Prepare reactions as described in the qPCR mixture step, using both knock‑in and reference primer sets for each sample (duplicate or triplicate wells). Run the program: 98 °C 2 min; 50 cycles of 98 °C 15 s, 60 °C 2 min. Collect Ct values.

steps.title: Calculate HR activity (ΔΔCt)
steps.instruction: For homogeneous samples compute ΔΔCt using Formula 1 and convert to relative knock‑in efficiency with Formula 2 (2^(‑ΔΔCt)). For heterogeneous samples compute ΔΔCt with Formula 3 and use –ΔΔCt as the HR activity metric.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been used and validated in the following research articles: • Yoshino et al. [12]. Evaluation of site-specific homologous recombination activity of BRCA1 by direct quantitation of gene editing efficiency. Scientific Reports (Figures 4 and 6). • Endo et al. [9]. BRCA1/ATF1-Mediated Transactivation is Involved in Resistance to PARP Inhibitors and Cisplatin. Cancer Research Communications ( Figures 1 , 2 , 4, and 6). • Motonari et al. [13]. Evaluating homologous recombination activity in tissues to predict the risk of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer and olaparib sensitivity. Scientific Reports ( Figures 2 and 5). • Yanaihara et al. [15]. Paclitaxel sensitizes homologous recombination-proficient ovarian cancer cells to PARP inhibitor via the CDK1/BRCA1 pathway. Gynecologic Oncology ( Figures 1D , 2D , 3C, 3D). • Iida et al. [16]. Bevacizumab increases the sensitivity of olaparib to homologous recombination-proficient ovarian cancer by suppressing CRY1 via PI3K/AKT pathway. Frontiers in Oncology ( Figure 2A , E, and F).
